LESSON: INSPIRED WORD OF GOD

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Bible
Topic 2.1: Inspired Word of God

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Inspired Word of God. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is the Bible different from other books?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain why the Bible is the inspired word of God
2. name three authors who wrote the Bible
3. discuss reasons that led to translation of the Bible into local languages
4. read the Bible always to get spiritual nourishment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INSPIRED WORD OF GOD
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Inspired Word of God helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: INSPIRED WORD OF GOD
Study Inspired Word of God like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain why the Bible is the inspired word of God

What this means
In this part you learn to explain why the Bible is the inspired word of God. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain why the Bible is the inspired word of God.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Inspired Word of God” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain why the Bible is the inspired word of God. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Name three authors who wrote the Bible

What this means
In this part you learn to name three authors who wrote the Bible. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: name three authors who wrote the Bible.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Inspired Word of God in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can name three authors who wrote the Bible. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Discuss reasons that led to translation of the Bible into local languages

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss reasons that led to translation of the Bible into local languages. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss reasons that led to translation of the Bible into local languages.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss reasons that led to translation of the Bible into local languages. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Read the Bible always to get spiritual nourishment

What this means
In this part you learn to read the Bible always to get spiritual nourishment. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read the Bible always to get spiritual nourishment.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Inspired Word of God” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read the Bible always to get spiritual nourishment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Inspired Word of God is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Inspired Word of God” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain why the Bible is the inspired word of God)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Inspired Word of God in your own words. (skill: name three authors who wrote the Bible)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: discuss reasons that led to translation of the Bible into local languages)

Example 4: Show how “Inspired Word of God” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: read the Bible always to get spiritual nourishment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Inspired Word of God to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain why the Bible is the inspired word of God.
3. Practise this skill: name three authors who wrote the Bible.
4. Practise this skill: discuss reasons that led to translation of the Bible into local languages.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Inspired Word of God from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Inspired Word of God: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Inspired Word of God?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is the Bible different from other books?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Inspired Word of God means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain why the Bible is the inspired word of God.
5. Be able to: name three authors who wrote the Bible.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
